tooltip-marketplace-ticker-disclaimer: The products displayed below are those with status changes in the last 30 days. FedRAMP does not endorse any product.
tooltip-csp-content-disclaimer: Disclaimer: FedRAMP does not review or endorse vendor-submitted content. Vendors are responsible for accuracy of product descriptions, provided services, and contact information.
tooltip-authorizing-agency: The sponsoring government agency for this FedRAMP authorized cloud service offering. Relevant for Rev5 Agency certifications.
tooltip-assessor: An independent entity that performs the initial and periodic assessment of cloud service offerings to ensure they meet FedRAMP requirements.
tooltip-assessment-date: The date when an independent assessor assessed this cloud service offering to ensure it is following FedRAMP requirements.
tooltip-uei: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number is a unique organization id administered by the System for Award Management (sam.gov), operated by the General Services Administration (GSA).
tooltip-business-categories: The classification of the purpose of a Cloud Service Offering (CSO). CSOs may self-identify up to 10 business categories from a non-exhaustive list, please review the Service Description section for supporting information.
tooltip-service-model: A cloud service offering's cloud business model: Software as a Service (SaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and/or Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS).
tooltip-deployment-model: The cloud deployment model this cloud service offering is hosted on: Public, Private, Hybrid, Community, or Multi-Cloud.
tooltip-marketplace-status: Indicates the current stage of this cloud service offering within the FedRAMP Marketplace lifecycle. Stages include: Initial Implementation, (Legacy) FedRAMP Ready, Agency Authorization In Process, FedRAMP In Process, or FedRAMP Certified.
tooltip-package-id: Unique FedRAMP-assigned ID for this cloud service offering's Security Package.
tooltip-certification-class: Describes the amount of documentation provided by the cloud service provider and level of commitment for ongoing maintenance and reporting activities for a FedRAMP Certification. In order of increasing requirements, there are Class A, B, C, and D Certifications.
tooltip-impact-level-deprecated: FedRAMP's general assessment of potential organizational impact if events compromise the information and systems necessary for agency mission.
tooltip-certification-type: 20x certification is a modern cloud-native approach that is new in 2026. Rev5 certification is a modified version of the legacy approach that will be retired in the future.
tooltip-certification-path: Program certification path is directly provided by the FedRAMP program. Agency certification path requires a federal agency to authorize the service in advance, following the legacy FedRAMP process.
tooltip-certification-profile: A summary of this cloud service offering's certification characteristics: its Type (20x or Rev5), its Path (Program or Agency), and its Class (A–D, reflecting documentation and ongoing reporting requirements).
tooltip-certified-since: The date this cloud service offering first became FedRAMP Certified. Shown only for certified offerings.
tooltip-authorization-type-deprecated: The specific FedRAMP Authorization type of this cloud service offering. Rev5 is the main authorization type. 20x is the new authorization type that will deprecate Rev5.
tooltip-authorizations: Total Authority to Operate (ATO) and/or Authority to Use (ATU) letters, including initial and reuse authorizations.
tooltip-reuses: Total Authority to Operate (ATO) and/or Authority to Use (ATU) letters plus any ATOs/ATUs granted to other FedRAMP Certified products leveraging this Cloud Service Offering (i.e., dependent products).
tooltip-phase: The current lifecycle phase of this cloud service offering: Legacy FedRAMP Ready (earned FedRAMP Ready under the legacy process, may now be pursuing a certification), Initial Implementation (standing up the offering), or Ongoing Certification (steady-state continuous monitoring and reporting).
tooltip-corrective-action-plan: A Corrective Action Plan (CAP) documents findings the cloud service provider is actively remediating. A CSO operating under a CAP remains FedRAMP Certified while it addresses these findings.
